item.title: VP Chiwenga pushes explosives production drive as mining demand surges
item.description: Vice President Constantino Chiwenga has called for stronger collaboration between industry, academic institutions and Government to boost local explosives production, warning that continued reliance on imports could undermine Zimbabwe’s rapidly expanding mining sector.

item.title: A Silobela nurse appeals for road rehab
item.description: A nurse from Silobela Hospital is highlighting the need for road rehabilitation due to challenging conditions affecting access to healthcare.

item.title: Zimbabweans abroad: Uber drivers in Cape Town
item.description: I took a lot of Uber rides while there and virtually all drivers (bar two Malawians) were Zimbabweans.

item.title: Zimbabwe – our very own Animal Farm!
Zimbabwe Vigil Diary 7th March 2026
item.description: Once again Vigil activists met outside the Zimbabwe Embassy in London to continue our protest against the human rights abuse and lack of democracy in Zimbabwe perpetrated by ZANU PF, the ruling regime.

item.title: ZIMSEC Sets Deadline For 2026 O’ And A’ Level Exam Registrations
item.description: The Zimbabwe School Examinations Council (ZIMSEC) has set 27 March 2026 as the deadline for registering candidates for the November 2026 Ordinary and Advanced Level exams.

item.title: Fuzwayo Withdraws Court Challenge Against ZANU PF’s 2030 Agenda
item.description: Bulawayo-based political activist Mbuso Fuzwayo and his pressure group, Ibhetshu Likazulu, have withdrawn their Constitutional Court challenge against the proposed Constitutional Amendment Number 3, which seeks to extend President Emmerson Mnangagwa’s term beyond 2028. The withdrawal takes effect immediately.

item.title: Lawyers Keep USD450 000 Legal Fees
item.description: Lawyers involved in Matabeleland pressure group Ibhetshu LikaZulu and secretary-general Mbuso Fuzwayo's Constitutional Court bid to block President Emmerson Mnangagwa's term extension will keep their staggering legal fees involving US$450 000 despite their client withdrawing the case in a shock move this afternoon, an insider said.

item.title: Jonathan Moyo Reacts To Ibhetshu LikaZulu Move
item.description: Exiled former minister and MP Jonathan Moyo, now a ruling Zanu PF political strategist, has replied to questions sent to him by The NewsHawks on Ibhetshu LikaZulu and its secretary-general Mbuso Fuzwayo's shock withdrawal of a Constitutional Court application challenging President Emmerson Mnangagwa's term extension and a series of contentious constitutional amendments changing the political, electoral and governance systems.
